approach.method_basis: The Parent generates fresh molecular graphs from current-session accepted molecules, then fits a count-kernel Gaussian process to a learned monotone transformation of their standardized scores. The transformation has one positive linear coefficient and three tanh terms, fitted by a bounded likelihood optimizer including the Jacobian. The inverse law turns correlated latent draws into raw-score draws; its quadrature expectation supplies the existing stalled top-forty eligibility rule. Accepted raw scores still update the archive, survivors and breeders. This learned law has already changed actual purchases, but one capped fit left a batch without predictions and the complete endpoint score fell.
approach.novelty: Replace the likelihood estimator and its acceptance rule with one deterministic constrained trust-region solve. Exact curvature guides its steps, and a separately recomputed gradient and projected first-order residual decide whether the result may supply predictions. This tests whether certified estimation can remove the coverage obstacle without changing the statistical model. The other scheduled siblings change noise, eligibility consumption or the fitted linear degree; none of those changes is included here.

Of the originally accepted fits, 125 report projected gradient above 0.001 and 13 above 0.1; the historical ftol acceptance is valid under its own rule and is not retrospectively relabeled. method_change.previous_method: Parent n-80d9b7174bc7 estimates its ten-parameter fixed-covariance warp with bounded L-BFGS-B and original solver-success plus initial-objective acceptance.
method_change.proposed_method: A single exact-Hessian constrained trust-region estimator of that identical objective and parameter box, followed by independent derivative, feasibility and projected first-order certification.
method_change.rationale: The Parent's one capped fit leaves the complete predictive test unanswered, while many accepted original fits used the permitted function-reduction stopping route with larger logged gradients. Changing the estimator and mathematical acceptance criterion targets this observed obstacle without replacing the learned output law, increasing resources or invalidating historical results.

hypothesis: Change only how the inherited ten-parameter monotone output law is estimated and admitted. On every original fitting occasion, use one fresh deterministic bound-constrained trust-constr run with the unchanged raw Jacobian-adjusted NLL, analytic gradient, exact analytic Hessian and original initial vector. A fit is eligible for active predictions only when independent objective/complex-step derivative agreement, exact box feasibility, finite values, original initial-objective slack and a projected-gradient mapping residual at most 1e-5 all pass. Solver success, mathematical certificate and nonlinear exposure are separate fields. This is the continuation's changed constrained estimator and acceptance certificate for the same fitted law, with no extra model choice or restart.

finding_summary.headline: Certification worked on 393 fits, but 42 missing laws leave the full predictive test unanswered.
finding_summary.insights: Native solver success and the registered mathematical certificate answer different questions: all 393 accepted fits ended through the certificate-candidate callback with native success false, whereas 40 native successes failed the independent residual threshold. Independent reconstruction confirms those decisions; this is not evidence that the certificate was bypassed or that the historical Parent’s different acceptance rule was invalid. The estimator and certificate operated as implemented, but their promised coverage repair failed, so the nonlinear law’s complete predictive hypothesis remains open. Favorable loss on observed pairs, a small code-Parent score gain, and first-order feasibility do not establish missing predictions, global likelihood optimality, or the unchanged formal-comparator goal. The source-derived likelihood and inverse law operated where accepted; fixed covariance and a learned linear coefficient remain campaign adaptations, so this is not a full reproduction of the literature model. The molecular report also shows a proposal limitation that numerical certification does not resolve: 152 accepted molecules exceeded fifty heavy atoms versus 59 in the Parent, alongside unusual heteroatom bonds and 2,540 molecules with possible unassigned stereocentres but no specified centres. More scaffold types in some streams did not consistently accompany endpoint gains. Graph operators that preserve chemical context and explicitly handle stereochemistry address this separate class of limitation; their benefit is untested here. Neither molecular descriptors nor available-pair predictive gains identify the cause of endpoint changes or settle the wider approach.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen task/seed sessions completed their observation budgets. Of 435 attempted fits, 393 passed the independent first-order certificate; 42 failed only its stationarity check and used the inherited generation-order fallback. This leaves 3,930 of 4,350 purchases with prospective laws, versus the Parent’s 4,340. All 393 accepted laws were nonlinear, and 385 pools changed their purchased set relative to the same-state passive raw GP. On the available 3,930 pairs, active mean pinball was 0.0163671 versus 0.0193968; those incomplete denominators prevent a conclusion about the registered complete-stream prediction. The mean endpoint score was 0.5744836979760076 versus the code Parent’s 0.57216721801385, a trusted paired gain of 0.0023164799621576693. Two seed macros declined and one improved; six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved, with the largest gain concentrated in one sitagliptin session. The formal comparator remained higher at 0.607030316211131, with a paired difference of -0.03254661823512336. Full/late generating-parent gains were 17.71294/4.53228 versus the code Parent’s 18.15524/5.40550, while total incumbent increments were 5.48987 versus 5.45513. These local-gain diagnostics describe different adaptive streams and are separate from the endpoint comparison.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and amine-bearing frameworks persist, with a larger size tail, unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The complete Child and code Parent each provide fifteen legal Search task/seed trajectories: 4,500 accepted records, including 150 initial records and 4,350 optimizer records. Child completeness and Parent pairing are both true; no task, seed or comparison path is missing. This assessment concerns the accepted molecules, not rejected proposals or unpurchased internal pools. The chemical baseline is n-80d9b7174bc7; the formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains a separate comparator and is not re-assessed chemically here. The frozen macro means are 0.5744836979760076 and 0.57216721801385, with signed paired delta 0.0023164799621576693. The seed macro deltas are -0.014576314191799944, +0.03670981519432892 and -0.015184061116055969. These are supplied descriptive score results, not a ranking, activation finding or Anchor-goal conclusion. Both nodes generate substantial ring chemistry with aromatic, amide, amine, ether and heterocyclic arrangements. RDKit finds rings in 4,292/4,350 Child optimizer rows versus 4,289/4,350 Parent rows, and aromatic atoms in 4,069 versus 4,185. The Child has 42 <=5-heavy-atom rows versus Parent 61, but 152 >50-heavy-atom rows versus Parent 59. N–halogen/O–halogen/O–O single-bond/terminal N–S row counts are 363/183/83/107 versus Parent 425/377/220/48; these categories overlap and are graph features, not calibrated chemical-risk scores. Possible unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2,540 Child and 2,421 Parent rows, with zero specified-centre rows on either side. The five Child digest ring-closure text rates, in task order, are 0.9966/0.9839/0.9897/0.9966/0.9667; aromatic text rates are 0.9908/0.9839/0.9851/0.9954/0.7218. All digest charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0. These digest counters are SMILES-string readings, distinct from the RDKit 2023.09.6 graph measurements. RDKit graph validity, scaffold variety and low fingerprint similarity do not establish feasible synthesis, stability, biological usefulness or causal mediation of score changes. The quality labels below are qualitative readings: many familiar medicinal motifs coexist with unusual bond contexts and complex ring closures. Typed/generic scaffold counts exclude empty Murcko scaffolds. Similarity uses Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits, no chirality; both generated and initial sets exclude disconnected or <=5-heavy-atom structures. No model fitting or oracle call was performed. Summary and definitions: policy/scratch/r0068-00-improve-L01-molecular/molecular-panel-summary.json. Immutable request: policy/requests/r0068-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-bb2a88e8ed9e3796.json. Every per-task source citation includes the original published Parent trajectory and a byte-identical preserved Child trajectory, whose trusted original staging path and SHA256 are recorded in the audit.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
